notes: The actual crux - constructing a single file that both python3 and gcc accept by abusing comment/string/preprocessor overlap - has essentially no analogue in any corpus; regex sweeps for polyglot-source / valid-in-two-languages / quine found only JS quines (RTS, TW) and file-format 'polyglot' security tasks. BEWARE the dominant false positive: the word 'polyglot' appears on many TMax and RTS tasks that mean a multi-language *pipeline* (C/Go/Rust + Python via FFI/build), not a single dual-valid source - I did not let that lexical match inflate scores; those earn points only for genuine C-and-Python-must-agree content. I decomposed the task into three transferable sub-skills and scored on them: (a) implement the same Fibonacci in C and Python and make them agree (TMax's Fibonacci-polyglot cluster: task_009068/006029/004333/005942), (b) reconcile Python and C semantics (SWE-Rebench's pyccel Python-to-C transpiler - the single best non-TMax find, surfaced by my own search not the shortlist), and (c) construct source under an unusual dual-validity/self-reference constraint (quines) plus C-preprocessor abuse (tw_730164) and cross-language interop (tw_12315). No candidate anywhere teaches the gzip-free, comment-trick core, and the task itself is small/single-step, so even the best matches are overall 3, not 4-5. SWE-Smith's contribution (parso/flake8/pygments = Python-grammar and multi-language-lexing awareness) is weak, overall 2 at best. Merge note: expect other agents' shortlists here to be polluted by 'polyglot pipeline' boilerplate matches; the honest signal is Fibonacci-in-C+Python and the pyccel transpiler line.
